waves.name: Wave 2
waves.why: The storefront, its builder and the rules that drive it
waves.bn: দোকানের সামনের অংশ, পেজ সাজানোর টুল, কম্বো আর দোকানের নিয়ম।

waves.name: Wave 3
waves.why: The money path, end to end
waves.bn: টাকার পথ শুরু থেকে শেষ: ব্যাগ, checkout, অর্ডার, পেমেন্ট আর কুরিয়ার।

waves.name: Wave 4
waves.why: Everything around an order once it exists

waves.name: Wave 5

waves.name: Wave 6

waves.bn: AI কন্ট্রোল রুম, হিসাব-রিপোর্ট আর সাইটের স্বাস্থ্য।

waves.name: Wave 7
waves.why: Imagery, once the catalogue is real
waves.bn: ক্যাটালগ তৈরি হলে ছবি আর ভিডিও বানানোর স্টুডিও।

waves.name: Wave 8
waves.bn: একাধিক দোকান, নিয়মকানুন আর নতুন দোকান চালু (go-live)।

waves.name: Parked

stages.name: Server foundation

bn.name: সার্ভারের ভিত্তি
bn.line: দোকান যে সার্ভারে চলবে, সেটা গুছিয়ে তৈরি করা — নিরাপত্তা, ডাটাবেস, ব্যাকআপ আর নজরদারি।
summary: Azure-এর নতুন সার্ভারে দোকান চালানোর সব ব্যবস্থা এই ধাপে।
নিরাপত্তা, ডাটাবেস, ক্যাশ, HTTPS, রোজকার ব্যাকআপ আর সমস্যা হলে খবর — সব এখানে।
নতুন কোড এলে সাইট বন্ধ না করেই চালু হয়; সমস্যা হলে নিজে থেকে আগের ভার্সনে ফেরে।

stages.name: Foundation — repo, CI, schema, auth, settings framework

bn.name: ভিত্তি — কোড, সেটিংস আর লগইন
bn.line: সব কাজের গোড়া: কোডের কাঠামো, ডাটাবেসের নকশা, সেটিংস, চাবির লকার আর অ্যাডমিন লগইন।
summary: পুরো দোকানের ডাটাবেসের নকশা একবারে বানানো, যাতে পরে ভাঙতে না হয়।
কোনো নাম, দাম বা নিয়ম কোডে লেখা থাকে না — সব সেটিংস থেকে আসে, অ্যাডমিন থেকে বদলানো যায়।
API চাবি তালাবন্ধ লকারে থাকে; স্টাফ লগইন, রোল আর পারমিশনও এই ধাপে।

bn.line: পণ্য, রং, সাইজ, ক্যাটাগরি, সাইজ চার্ট আর ছবির সব কাজ।
summary: পণ্য যোগ, এডিট আর দোকানে তোলার অ্যাডমিন পাতা এই ধাপে।
ছবি আপলোড করলে নিজে থেকে 5টা সাইজে, দ্রুত লোড হওয়া ফরম্যাটে তৈরি হয়।
সব চেক পাস না করলে কোনো পণ্য দোকানে ওঠে না; সাইজ চার্ট, কালেকশন, CSV আর লিংক থেকে ইমপোর্টও আছে।

summary: কাস্টমার যে পাতাগুলো দেখে — হোম, ক্যাটাগরি, পণ্যের পাতা, সার্চ — সব এই ধাপে।

পেজ সাজানো, লেখা বদলানো আর থিম — সব অ্যাডমিন থেকে করা যাবে।

সেটের দাম আর আলাদা কেনার চেয়ে কত বাঁচল, তা পরিষ্কার দেখাবে।

bn.line: ভুয়া আর ডুপ্লিকেট অর্ডার ধরা, আর ঠিকানা দেখে সঠিক ডেলিভারি চার্জ বের করা।
summary: ভুয়া বা ডুপ্লিকেট অর্ডার ধরার নিয়ম, কিন্তু আসল কাস্টমারের অর্ডার কখনো আটকাবে না।
কাউকে নিজে থেকে ব্লক করা হয় না — মানুষ দেখে সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়।
সারা দেশের এলাকার তালিকা থেকে ঠিকানা মিলিয়ে সঠিক ডেলিভারি চার্জ।

bn.name: পেমেন্ট আর ওয়ালেট
bn.line: ক্যাশ অন ডেলিভারি, bKash, Nagad, কার্ড আর কাস্টমারের ওয়ালেট।
summary: COD, bKash, Nagad আর কার্ডে টাকা নেওয়ার ব্যবস্থা।
চাবি না আসা পর্যন্ত প্রতিটা পেমেন্ট সংযোগ নকল (mock) মোডে চলবে।
ওয়ালেটে টাকা ফেরত আর পেমেন্টের হিসাব মেলানোর রিপোর্ট।

bn.name: কুরিয়ার, ফেরত আর এক্সচেঞ্জ
bn.line: কুরিয়ার বুকিং, স্টিকার, পিকিং লিস্ট, প্যাকিং, ট্র্যাকিং আর এক্সচেঞ্জ।
summary: Steadfast আর অন্য কুরিয়ারে বুকিং, স্টিকার প্রিন্ট আর রোজকার পিকিং লিস্ট।
কোন কুরিয়ারে খরচ কম, সেটা দেখে বাছাই — কাস্টমারের চার্জ তাতে বদলায় না।
এক্সচেঞ্জ, ফেরত আসা পার্সেল আর কুরিয়ারের পারফরম্যান্স রিপোর্ট।

notes.text: No new PR numbers: scope lands on the existing S02/S03/S04/S05/S08/S14/S16/S20/S22 PRs.

bn.name: স্টক আর ERP সংযোগ
bn.line: আপনার ERP থেকে স্টক আনা, অর্ডার ERP-তে পাঠানো আর গুদামের হিসাব।
summary: স্টকের আসল হিসাব থাকে আপনার ERP-তে; দোকান সেখান থেকে SKU আর সাইজ ধরে স্টক আনে।
একই শেষ পিস দুজনের কাছে বিক্রি হয় না; অর্ডার ERP-তে ডকুমেন্ট হিসেবে যায়, একবারই।
ERP-এর চাবি না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত একটা প্র্যাকটিস ERP চলে, আসল স্টকে হাত দেয় না।

bn.name: স্মার্ট নিয়ম
bn.line: ডেলিভারি চার্জ, এক্সচেঞ্জ, সেটের দাম, কুপন আর উৎসবের নিয়ম — সব এক জায়গা থেকে।
summary: দোকানের নিয়মগুলো (ডেলিভারি, এক্সচেঞ্জ, সেটের দাম, কুপন) এক জায়গায় সেট করা যাবে।
নিয়ম বদলালে সাইটের সব জায়গার লেখা নিজে থেকে বদলে যাবে।
নতুন নিয়ম চালুর আগে দেখা যাবে, আগের অর্ডারে তাতে কী হতো।

bn.name: SEO — গুগলে খুঁজে পাওয়া
bn.line: গুগল, Bing আর AI অ্যাসিস্ট্যান্টে দোকান খুঁজে পাওয়ার সব কাজ।
summary: পাতার লিংক, টাইটেল, sitemap আর গুগলের জন্য তথ্য ঠিকমতো সাজানো।
বাংলা পাতা আলাদা /bn/ লিংকে; অনুবাদ ঠিক হলে তবেই চালু।
কোনো পণ্যের লিংক কখনো মরে না; পুরনো লিংক নতুনটায় চলে যায়।

notes.text: Bengali pages get their own /bn/ URLs with hreflang for Google traffic (S11)

bn.name: কনটেন্ট আর ব্লগ
bn.line: ব্লগ, গাইড আর হেল্প আর্টিকেল — গুগল থেকে কাস্টমার আনার জন্য।
summary: কাপড়ের যত্ন, স্টাইল আর ফেব্রিক নিয়ে নিয়মিত ব্লগ পোস্ট।
AI এজেন্ট লেখে, আরেকজন যাচাই করে, তারপর প্রকাশ হয়।
কোন লেখা থেকে কত বিক্রি হলো, তার হিসাব থাকবে।

bn.name: মার্কেটিং আর বিজ্ঞাপন
bn.line: ল্যান্ডিং পেজ, Facebook/Google/TikTok বিজ্ঞাপন, কুপন আর অসমাপ্ত অর্ডার ফিরিয়ে আনা।
summary: ক্যাম্পেইনের ল্যান্ডিং পেজ আর Facebook, Google, TikTok বিজ্ঞাপনের সংযোগ।
বিজ্ঞাপনের হিসাব হয় আসলে ডেলিভারি হওয়া অর্ডার ধরে।
কুপন, রেফারেল আর অসমাপ্ত অর্ডার বা ফেলে রাখা ব্যাগ ফিরিয়ে আনার মেসেজ।

bn.name: কাস্টমার আর CRM
bn.line: কাস্টমারের তালিকা, ইতিহাস, মেসেজ, রিভিউ আর রিওয়ার্ড।

changeNotes.title: owner: one README a developer can read in five years
changeNotes.text: (Filed as CN-011 because CN-010 is held by owner Note 53 in open GitHub PR #18.) (1) **README is the live, detailed front page** (`README.md`: status dashboard of all 28 stages, how it is built, local setup, the server, folder structure, features by area, PR log, change notes, docs map, notes for a future developer; `docs/README.md` indexes every docs file). After **every** merged PR the build agent updates the dashboard, adds the PR log row and updates the feature section of that area. (2) **Docs on the server:** every deploy copies the repo's `docs/` (with `README.md`, `BLUEPRINT.md`, `MASTER-REGISTER.md`) to the server, one way (repo → server), so the admin's "PR register" and "Blueprint & files" tabs (PR 594) always show the latest. (3) **Docs in backups:** every backup (PR 8 / 395 / 507; Azure Blob and Google Drive) carries a dated docs bundle — `README.md`, `docs/BLUEPRINT.md`, `docs/MASTER-REGISTER.md` and the whole `docs/` folder, with the commit hash — so a restore brings back the documentation of that exact version. (4) **Organisation standard, kept in every PR:** standard code style (lint and format checks), tests beside the code, clear names, a short header comment on each package saying what it is for, `docs/` kept current, and the blueprint and register changed only through CN notes. No new PR numbers: (1) is the S00 routine of PR 11, (2) lands on PR 4/17 (`deploy.yml`, `infra/deploy/deploy.sh`) and PR 594, (3) on PR 8, 395 and 507, (4) on PR 11 and 17.

(2) **Checkout texts and field order are settings** (heading "Delivery details", labels, the Bengali address hint, the exchange-for-size link, the try-on line), as are the bag-panel style (default and B), the recommendation fill rule (as many as fit, ≥12 px under the buttons, then "+N more"), payment options (COD open, Mobile/Card/Online payment on click) and the logo choice. (3) **Phone rule:** text changes reach the phone; a design change reaches the phone only after the device gate and phone pixel diff prove 0 side effects. (2) **Open boundary, every PR and stage:** each finding or feature gets the fix, prevention, a review of the core decision and growth ideas (easier, smarter, more profitable), recorded in the stage report; ideas on money, prices, COD or blocking are proposals for the owner (hard rule 6). changeNotes.title: owner: add the 8 best simulation ideas as optional settings; a Bengali guide per admin section
changeNotes.text: (1) Eight ideas from `docs/qa/SIMULATION-PLAN.md` §7 are added. Each is **off by default**, has its own on/off switch, and every number in it can be edited. Each lives in the admin section it belongs to; no new top-level menu. (a) **WhatsApp self-confirm** (idea 5): the reply 1/2/3 texts, the hours to wait before the call queue, and which orders it applies to. Section: Orders → Confirmation. Scope on PR 148, 292 and 545. (b) **Exact-amount line** (idea 10) on the sticker, SMS and tracking page, with the text and the report link. Section: Messages + Shipping labels. Scope on PR 179, 148 and 135. (c) **Packing proof photo** (idea 13): required or optional, and how many days to keep it. Section: Fulfilment. Scope on PR 182. (d) **RTO cost book** (idea 8): cost per RTO (courier charge, packaging, staff), by district, campaign, product, courier and reason. Section: Reports. Scope on PR 164, 192 and 267. (e) **One-trip size swap** (idea 17): the swap charge and the eligible areas. Section: Exchanges. Scope on PR 190. (f) **Day-1 WhatsApp care** (idea 15): the send hour, the text, and the Day-3 review request. Section: Messages. Scope on PR 295, 289 and 505. (g) **Eid order-by dates per district** (idea 19): the dates, the bands, the banner text, and pre-order with an advance amount. Section: Campaigns. Scope on PR 193 and 214. (h) **Gift mode** (idea 22): receiver name and phone, hide prices on the invoice, a gift note, and a "deliver on or after" date. Section: Checkout settings. This is the next free PR in S04. All 24 ideas stay listed in the plan, and the other 16 wait for the owner. (2) **Admin section guide (Bengali, a blueprint).** `docs/admin-guide/` holds one Bengali file per admin section (plain চলতি Bengali, Western digits) and an index. Each file says what the section is for, every menu and tab in it, what can be done there, every switch and number with its default, and what happens next. It is shown in the admin too, as a "এই সেকশনে কী করা যায়" help link on each section. **Every PR that adds or changes an admin screen updates its guide in the same PR** (same rule as README, CN-011). No other new PR numbers: (2) is the S00 routine of PR 11 plus PR 594's "Blueprint & files" tab.

changeNotes.title: owner: customer problems are found automatically, a "Running problems" list in the admin and at the top of README
changeNotes.text: (1) **Detect from real visits.** On every page and step of the journey (landing → product → bag → checkout → tracking → account), a small privacy-safe browser probe and server checks record: script errors, failed or slow requests, pages that fail to load, payment and API failures, stuck or repeated form errors (for example the phone field failing three times), "rage" clicks and dead clicks, checkout abandoned right after an error, slow loads by device and network type, and broken images. Each record carries the device, browser, network, area (district only) and journey step. **No name, phone, address or payment detail is ever recorded.** Visitor ids are random. (2) **Group and judge.** The backend groups records with the same cause into one **problem**, counts the visitors and orders it hit, estimates the lost sales, and marks it Urgent / Important / Can wait, with a plain Bengali summary of what went wrong, where and for whom. Short glitches that fixed themselves are kept too, under "short glitches". (3) **Status for each problem:** New · Fixing · Fixed (with how) · Could not fix (why) · Needs owner permission · Fixed, waiting for the owner's check before going live. (4) **Auto-fix:** when a fix touches no hard-rule item (money, prices, COD, blocking, deleting data) and needs no owner permission, the build agent fixes it through a normal PR (tests and gates, then merge), writes the note, and the problem moves to Fixed. Otherwise the problem goes to Needs owner permission. (5) **Where the owner sees it:** the admin **Site health → Customer problems** page (with the Server page, PR 423), which has a date view (today, yesterday, any day, trend) and a detail page for each problem; and the **top of README.md**, under "Running problems", with one line per open problem (date, short title, users hit, status) linking to `docs/problems/<id>.md` for details. Both are refreshed automatically by a scheduled workflow, with the problem data anonymised before it is written to GitHub. (6) **Sales link:** the weekly report says which problems most likely cost sales. No new PR numbers: it lands on S21 (PR 413–424, mainly PR 423 and the audit runner PR 570), PR 594 and the README routine (CN-011). Some parts are moved earlier: the probe and the problem list start as soon as the shop's checkout exists on new.extas.com.bd, so the simulation and staging tests feed it too.

changeNotes.title: owner: nothing reaches the owner broken
changeNotes.text: The owner found that after logging in, the admin on new.extas.com.bd showed "This page couldn't load". New gate: **after every deploy and every night**, a smoke test runs on the runner with Playwright against new.extas.com.bd. It signs in with a check account whose password lives only on the server, then visits every built storefront page and every built admin page, including the pages right after login. A page passes only when it loads, shows no error screen and no console error, and has no failed request. If any page fails, the deploy rolls back by itself and the fix comes before any new PR. Screenshots go to `docs/reports/smoke/latest/`, and the result is shown on the status page and in README. Every bug the owner finds gets a smoke check in the same fix PR. No new PR numbers: this lands on PR 4/17 (deploy) and Appendix C.

updates.text: **Updated 19 Oct 23:33 (owner server spec): Azure Blob is added** (supersedes "Drive only, no Blob"). **Blob:** continuous WAL archive for point-in-time restore to any minute; daily full backups; soft delete and versioning or immutability on, so a mistake or ransomware cannot wipe it; images and media in Blob with soft delete and versioning. **Google Drive stays mandatory:** the daily full encrypted copy, off-site with a different company; the second add-only Drive is a third copy. prs.title: NVMe temporary-disk boot unit — format and mount at every boot, folder layout, systemd ordering before services, admin NVMe card and …
prs.scope: **NVMe temporary-disk boot unit (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** On the E8ds_v6 the 440 GB local NVMe is **raw**: after a stop, deallocate, maintenance or move it comes up unformatted (Microsoft docs). A systemd unit runs at **every boot, before Redis, Postgres and Docker start**: detect the NVMe → format it ext4 if it is not already → mount at `/mnt/nvme` → create the folder layout (Redis working cache, image-processing intermediates, studio rendering, Postgres `temp_tablespaces`, build and pnpm caches, backup staging, session/queue scratch) → set ownership. Those services wait for the unit to succeed (systemd ordering). It holds temporary items only — **never** the database, code, uploads, final backups or kept logs. **Admin:** an NVMe card (mounted or not, free space, which services use it, PR 423); a Telegram alert if it is missing (PR 9). Pre-launch required.

prs.title: Hardware-aware auto profile and run-anywhere — limits from detected CPU and RAM, storage adapter (local / Blob / S3), CDN optional (owner …
prs.scope: **Hardware-aware auto profile and run-anywhere (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** Every RAM/CPU limit lives in **one config file, never in code**. On this box: PostgreSQL 16 GB / 2–3 CPU · Redis 6 GB / 1 CPU · Meilisearch 4 GB · Node/Next.js 16 GB / 4–6 CPU, 6 replicas · image/video worker 6 GB / 2 CPU · background jobs 4 GB / 1 CPU · Caddy 1 GB / 1 CPU · OS and the rest 11 GB, never squeezed = 64 GB. The profile **detects CPU and RAM and computes the limits itself** on any other machine (for example 4 vCPU / 16 GB) — no hand edits. **Run-anywhere:** a storage adapter (local disk / Azure Blob / S3-compatible) on the adapter framework of PR 18, so the shop works **without Blob**; it works **without the CDN** (images served from the server); handover-ready (S26). The admin shows each service's RAM and CPU against its limit (PR 423). Pre-launch required.

prs.scope: **Database performance pack (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** Built with the schema (PR 13). **Required indexes:** category page (category + store + in-stock + sort, one index); SKU and variant by colour and size; order by phone (runs on every order for the fraud engine); fuzzy name/address with **`pg_trgm`** (the fraud/duplicate engine, PR 519); customer order history; style hierarchy for profit (Polo → brand polo → solid polo, PR 536); order list filters (date, status, courier, store). **Slow query log** for anything over 100 ms, target under 50 ms for a normal query, and an admin **"slowest queries"** page (PR 423). **Reports** (profit, ads, dashboard charts) run on **materialized views** refreshed on a schedule, or on a low-priority report pool, so they never slow the shop. Site search stays on Meilisearch (PR 72). Pre-launch required — nothing deferred.

updates.source: Scope added to existing PRs (owner server spec, CN-001; review/SERVER-SETUP-SPEC-OWNER.md; new PR 601–604)
updates.text: **The filing** — the owner approved every point of the analysis at 23:33 and said: where two decisions conflict, take the best one. Four new PRs (601 NVMe boot unit and 604 hardware-aware profile in S0A, 603 database performance pack in S00, 602 four-layer cache in S02); the rest is dated scope on the PR lines below (PR 1, 3–10, 13, 18, 22, 24, 37, 72, 88, 234, 519). **Every server item is required before go-live** — the owner's "later" list (monitoring page, monthly speed measurement, report pre-computation) is not deferred; items that need the app schema are built with their stage and marked *pre-launch required*. **Build order inside S0A:** 1 record specs (PR 1) → 2 hardening and UFW (PR 3) → 3 NVMe boot unit (PR 601) → 4 data-disk LVM (PR 1/3) → 5 Docker (PR 4) → 6 hardware-aware profile (PR 604) → 7 Postgres, PgBouncer and Redis tuning (PR 5, 6) → 8 Caddy, Cloudflare and Origin …

prs.title: Site builder — the whole site dynamic (owner, 19 Oct 21:23: "like WordPress + Elementor, nothing fixed")
prs.scope: **Site builder — the whole site dynamic (owner, 19 Oct 21:23: "like WordPress + Elementor, nothing fixed").** From the backend, with preview before publish: **menus** (header nav / mega menu / phone menu / bottom bar — add, rename, reorder, hide, custom links, featured tile), **header** (announcement bar, icons on/off and order, logo), **footer** (columns, links, texts, contact block, social and payment marks), **categories and sub-categories** (create, rename, reorder, hide, image, intro, SEO), **product page blocks** (order and visibility of gallery, price row, colours, sizes, offers, buy-together, reviews, FAQ, care link), **content pages** (help, policies, about, careers, payment — rich text editor), **theme** (colours, fonts, spacing tokens with contrast check). Builds on PR 595 (home/category sections), 596 (side canvas) and 597 (launch default / snapshots / undo). Every change: draft → preview on phone/tablet/desktop → publish; per-device visibility; version history and undo. **Guardrails, not a blank canvas:** blocks snap to the responsive grid (no free pixel dragging that breaks phones), contrast and tap-size checks block bad publishes, checkout keeps its tested structure (texts, fields on/off and order editable; payment steps locked). Handover-ready: every default is data, a new owner configures everything here, the owner's own data never ships (PR 509).

prs.scope: **On-page edit mode (owner, 19 Oct 22:27–22:33, plan approved 100%).** Logged in as super admin, a thin bar on every storefront page turns on Edit mode (customers never see it): hover a section → outline + Edit; click → side panel with that section's settings (texts, prices, products, offer tiers, shimmer, hide); "+" between sections adds one; draft shown in place → Publish → undo. Same engine as the site builder (PR 598), two doors. On phone: a light version (texts and offers only, no drag). **Desktop change → "Apply to phone too?"** If yes: previews on the **10 phone screen sizes most used in Bangladesh** (the owner can pick any to check by hand) plus automatic checks (nothing cut, no sideways scroll, tap size, buy button above the fold); it goes to phone only after the checks pass and the owner approves. **AI mode:** when on, an AI reviewer agent tests the change across phones, tablets and desktops (layout, speed, conversion rules, customer impact) and returns a short report — "safe to publish" or "Boss, don't publish: …" with reasons and screenshots; when AI mode is off it says so and the owner's own check stands. Guardrails as PR 598; checkout payment steps locked.

prs.title: Four-layer cache plus invalidation — browser, Cloudflare, server page cache, Redis; purge rules; 15 s stock display with live checks at …
prs.scope: **Four-layer cache plus invalidation (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33).** **Browser** (images, CSS, JS, fonts for a long time, hashed file names) → **Cloudflare** (static files long; category and product pages for a few minutes, duration in settings; cart, checkout, account and admin never cached) → **server page cache** (built HTML for minutes, renewed the moment something changes) → **Redis** (settings, the Dhaka area list, products, categories, stock display). **Purge rules:** price change → that product, its category pages and the CDN; stock change → instantly; settings change → every place that setting is used; new product → category pages and the sitemap. **Stock:** the display cache lasts 15 s and every stock change event purges it at once; **add-to-bag and checkout always read live stock with a row lock (PR 198)** — nothing oversells. An admin **"Clear all cache"** button; cache hit %% on the Server page (PR 423). All durations are settings. Pre-launch required.
prs.filedUnder: S02 addition — four-layer cache (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33; CN-001)
prs.appendixTitle: Four-layer cache plus invalidation — browser, Cloudflare, server page cache, Redis; purge rules; 15 s stock display with live checks at bag and checkout; Clear all cache (owner server spec, 19 Oct 23:33)

prs.title: Advance-payment checkout mode — for a flagged customer only, and only once he has filled everything in: COD disappears, bKash, Nagad and …
prs.scope: **Advance-payment checkout mode** — for a flagged customer only, and only once he has filled everything in: COD disappears, bKash, Nagad and card open, with one neutral line — delivery charge in advance, or full advance, by layer. **Built as the same checkout page with the payment section swapped**, not a second page: one page to design, one page to test on mobile, and no chance of the two drifting apart. The customer is never shown a score or a reason.

prs.title: Silent address backfill — a customer who writes only "Road 12, House 42" gets the Inside/Outside Dhaka question, unless his phone number is…
prs.scope: **Silent address backfill** — a customer who writes only "Road 12, House 42" gets the Inside/Outside Dhaka question, **unless his phone number is already known**. Then nothing is shown, nothing is prefilled, what he typed stays as he typed it, and the full address we hold is attached to the order in the backend for packing. A new address always wins over the stored one — he may have moved, or be sending a gift.
prs.filedUnder: S04 additions — Parameter for Checkout (§60.9, 18 Oct)

updates.text: **The filing** — the owner approved every point of the analysis at 23:33 and said: where two decisions conflict, take the best one. Four new PRs (601 NVMe boot unit and 604 hardware-aware profile in S0A, 603 database performance pack in S00, 602 four-layer cache in S02); the rest is dated scope on the PR lines below (PR 1, 3–10, 13, 18, 22, 24, 37, 72, 88, 234, 519). **Every server item is required before go-live** — the owner's "later" list (monitoring page, monthly speed measurement, report pre-computation) is not deferred; items that need the app schema are built with their stage and marked *pre-launch required*. **Build order inside S0A:** 1 record specs (PR 1) → 2 hardening and UFW (PR 3) → 3 NVMe boot unit (PR 601) → 4 data-disk LVM (PR 1/3) → 5 Docker (PR 4) → 6 hardware-aware profile (PR 604) → 7 Postgres, PgBouncer and Redis tuning (PR 5, 6) → 8 Caddy, Cloudflare and Origin …

prs.title: Ambiguity resolver — reads the whole line, and waits
prs.scope: **Ambiguity resolver — reads the whole line, and waits.** Nothing is decided while the cursor is still in the address field: people write the district a few words later ("Gabtoli Bus Stand, **Dhaka**"; "Masterpara, Gabtali, **Bogura**"). On blur, or a long enough pause, the resolver reads the complete address — a district, parent area or postcode anywhere in it settles the band **silently, with no question**. A postcode settles it (1216 Dhaka, 5820 Bogura); a co-occurring local name narrows it; a returning customer's saved address outranks any guess. **Only a line still ambiguous after that full read asks**, and once the customer confirms, nothing silently changes it.
prs.filedUnder: S06 additions — the delivery-zone engine (§60, 18 Oct)
prs.appendixTitle: Ambiguity resolver — reads the whole line, and waits

status.note: sync layer: per-call timeout, retry with exponential backoff and jitter (`erp.sync.*`: tries, base, cap, jitter), Retry-After honoured, AUTH and bad requests never retried, the checkout check never retried; error surface on ErpSyncRun (status, counts, one-line `CODE status: message (N tries)`) and ErpSyncState (`lastError`, cleared by the next good run), read by `GET /api/admin/inventory/erp` and later the PR 205 panel; a key never appears in an error

prs.bn: ERP-এর সাথে কথা বলার স্তর: টাইমআউট, আবার চেষ্টা, আর ভুল হলে সহজ ভাষায় কারণ।

prs.title: Stock pull from the ERP at SKU / colour / size level
prs.scope: Stock pull from the ERP at SKU / colour / size level
prs.appendixTitle: Stock pull from the ERP at SKU / colour / size level

status.note: stock pull per SKU / colour / size into StockLevel (variant × location): incremental with `updatedSince` minus an overlap, paged, resumable after a failure or the page cap; older rows never overwrite newer; one StockMovement per change with an idempotency key from the ERP's state (re-reading never moves stock twice); unknown / retired SKUs and unlinked warehouses counted, never guessed; `inStock` and the product summary follow; checkout check (`liveStock`, one quick try, else the copy); job functions for the BullMQ worker (`inventory.erp.pullStock`, poll every `erp.sync.stockPollMinutes`); `GET /api/admin/inventory/stock` (one SKU in every location, or a product's colour × size grid)

prs.bn: SKU, রং আর সাইজ ধরে ERP থেকে স্টক আনা; একই বদল দুবার গোনা হয় না।

prs.title: companyId and warehouse mapping per store
prs.scope: `companyId` and warehouse mapping per store
prs.appendixTitle: companyId and warehouse mapping per store

status.note: company and warehouse mapping per store: the key decides the company — checked before every sync (a different company stops it with `COMPANY_MISMATCH`, nothing written), an empty mirror is filled from a real answer (audited), the practice company is shown, never saved; `Store.erpCompanyId` / StoreErpMapping stay owner data (owner-data check 0 findings); the store's ERP warehouse limits the pull; local warehouses link one-to-one to ERP warehouses; `/api/admin/inventory/erp/verify`, `/erp/warehouses`

prs.bn: দোকান কোন ERP কোম্পানি আর গুদামের, তা মেলানো; ভুল কোম্পানি হলে সিঙ্ক থামে।

prs.title: Global reservation across all three stores
prs.scope: **Global reservation across all three stores** on the one shared stock pool
prs.appendixTitle: Global reservation across all three stores

status.note: global reservation on the one shared stock pool (A4.4): a cart hold counts against the pool of every store at once, so two stores can never sell the same last piece; `holdCart` / `releaseCart` / `convertCart` / `releaseOrderHolds`; the hold is local and never pushed to the ERP; `available = onHand − reserved` kept per pool; hold length from `inventory.reservation.holdMinutes` / `holdMinutesSignedIn` (Bhandari B03: 15 / 20), converted holds kept `convertedHoldHours`; `holdSummary` on the PR 205 panel. Storefront and checkout callers arrive with S04

prs.title: Blog content pipeline (owner, 19 Oct 12:10–12:14)
prs.scope: **Blog content pipeline (owner, 19 Oct 12:10–12:14)** — the blog is the main traffic engine: everyday fashion knowledge (care, washing, styling, fabrics, fit, occasions and seasons) plus our own product posts, **at least 3 and up to 5–6 posts a day**. In the backend: a topic list that Doot builds from real search demand (the owner can add topics and approve the list); Doot writes each post; **a second agent proofreads and fact-checks before it can publish** (writer never approves own post); interlinking rules (article → category/product, product → care guide, cluster links), SEO checklist, own photos, Bengali twin when ready (PR 588); a schedule that spreads posts through the day; a duplicate-topic check; per-post traffic and sales report. Quality is the system's job, not the owner's.

prs.appendixTitle: Blog content pipeline (owner, 19 Oct 12:10–12:14)

Byline: "EXTAS Journal" with the author agent name and the expert reviewer the owner enters.

prs.scope: **Blog as a complete, standard section of the shop, with our own ad placements (owner, 19 Oct 12:20).** Blog features: categories (pillars) and sub-categories, tags, author/reviewer pages, search, archive, featured and related posts, reading time, contents, share, RSS, newsletter sign-up, Bengali twins. **House ads only (no outside ad networks):** slots on the blog home (top banner, between cards), category pages, inside the article (after paragraph N, AdSense-style), sidebar on desktop, end of article, and an optional popup per post. Each ad is our banner, product, combo or category; the owner picks which ads show in which slots, posts and categories, with dates, weights and on/off. Popups have triggers (scroll %, time, leaving) and frequency caps, are easy to close, and by default don't open the moment a phone visitor lands from Google (Google's intrusive-interstitial guidance). Click and sales report per ad and slot.

prs.title: Chief agent — জ্ঞানী Gyani as virtual CEO (প্রধান এজেন্ট), chain of command
prs.scope: **Chief agent — জ্ঞানী Gyani as virtual CEO (প্রধান এজেন্ট), chain of command.** The owner charges one agent; Gyani answers to him and charges the other six by their performance. Asked "why are sales down this month / this week?", "why was today's courier entry wrong?", "why is this bug on the category page?", Gyani investigates across every section (orders, ads, stock, delivery, site errors, the agents' work logs), names **which agent's area caused it, with evidence**, assigns the fix to that agent, tracks it to done and reports back. Broad knowledge beyond its own stages (business, finance, operations, marketing, tech) — curriculum adds an executive/general-management track. Second only to the owner. **Free to do:** research, reports, analysis, assigning and reviewing work, warnings to agents (written into their appraisals PR 578). **Only with the owner's approval:** any money movement or refund, any COD amount change on an order, price or discount changes, ad budget increases, blocking anyone, deleting data, anything that cannot be undone. The permission list is a dashboard setting the owner edits; enforced by code. Lives in S15 AI 360 (org chart, open investigations, who-owns-what).

prs.title: Telegram identity and command routing
prs.scope: **Telegram identity and command routing.** All agents share the owner's one Telegram bot. Every message starts with the sender's identity — photo/emoji, name, Bengali name, **employee code**, role (e.g. "🏹 Tirondaj তীরন্দাজ · A360-07 · Ads") — so the owner always knows who sent it. When the owner writes a command naming an agent or its code ("A360-07 budget report", "@Bhandari courier entry check"), the task is **assigned to that agent automatically**, appears on its profile as an assignment, and the agent replies in the same thread when done. No name → goes to the chief (Gyani), who routes it. Approvals come back as buttons (Approve / Reject / Ask why). Also visible in the dashboard.

prs.title: Continuous learning engine — Tirondaj (ads) and Doot (SEO/marketing) are the two power agents
prs.scope: **Continuous learning engine — Tirondaj (ads) and Doot (SEO/marketing) are the two power agents.** They learn without stopping from: official docs (Meta, Google, TikTok, Search Central), the big practitioner blogs on SEO and paid ads, Reddit communities (PPC, Facebook ads, SEO, e-commerce), YouTube tutorials incl. South-Asian e-commerce channels (read through transcripts), LinkedIn and Facebook posts of known specialists (where readable; through a paid tool if needed), case studies. **When stuck:** research all sources → solve → the solution becomes a skill in its basket. **Quality gate (no shortcut learning):** a tip becomes a skill only after it is checked against the official docs or two independent good sources, tested in a sandbox or small live test, and written with its source, date and confidence; tips that fail are recorded as "doesn't work for us". **Practice tasks with deadlines** (e.g. get a new page indexed within 3 days, a long-tail keyword into Google's top 10, a test campaign under the CPA cap) graded in their appraisals. **Paid data tools** (e.g. an SEO suite) proposed with cost and reason — the owner approves and pays.

updates.text: (1) **Detect from real visits.** On every page and step of the journey (landing → product → bag → checkout → tracking → account), a small privacy-safe browser probe and server checks record: script errors, failed or slow requests, pages that fail to load, payment and API failures, stuck or repeated form errors (for example the phone field failing three times), "rage" clicks and dead clicks, checkout abandoned right after an error, slow loads by … — No new PR numbers: it lands on S21 (PR 413–424, mainly PR 423 and the audit runner PR 570), PR 594 and the README routine (CN-011). prs.title: PR register inside the backend (owner, 19 Oct 14:59)
prs.scope: **PR register inside the backend (owner, 19 Oct 14:59)** — an admin section listing every stage and every PR with its full details (what it does, scope added later and when, owner decision, status: built / parked / in demo / in code / live, owning agent, demo page link). Click a PR for the full card; search and filters; history of updates per PR (date, round, note); "report a problem on this PR" so the owner can point to an exact PR when something breaks — it opens a task for the owning agent via the chief. Generated from the master register on every build, so new PRs appear automatically; nothing typed twice. **Also holds the latest full blueprint .md (highest version marked latest), the master register and the supporting files** (round notes, plans, research, checklist, QA reports, agent protocol) — read inside the admin with contents and search, downloadable, with version history per file; backed up to Google Drive with everything else; no personal data, no third-party skill copies.
